judged_text: remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id), which is a silent no-op when user_id is not a member or does not exist, and no test covers that case. Stale UI state (member already removed in another tab) yields a 200 'success' with nothing deleted; the missing edge-case acceptance criterion means regressions here go undetected.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the new logic unconditionally does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds (which it likely will even if nothing changed). The accompanying specs under `context ".remove_member"` only cover (a) automatic group rejection and (b) removing an existing member; there is no test for attempting to remove a non-member / nonexistent user_id, so this edge-case behavior would go unverified.
